units.translation: The oracle will no longer be looking out from under veils.
and shamefully in the veils of the councilors
with fetters not forged by metal, when you were taken, father
rejoicing no less than in the Zeus-sent brightness, the seed in the birth-pangs of the husk
said by tmesis for κατακαλύψαι [to cover over].
The deep-black hiding-place of Tartarus covers ancient Cronus.
a tomb – I will contrive with this fold, carrying it of my linen robe, and I myself will cover him.
such as no Persian land ever covered
Would that, Zeus, you had covered me too in the fate of death.
The arts of Calchas are not unfulfilled.

corrupt word Suppl. 1002, where to the verse written by Aeschylus τέρειν᾽ ὀπώρα δ᾽ εὐφύλακτος οὐδαμῶς [tender fruit, but not at all well-guarded] an interpolator added four verses invented by himself, which are written thus in M, θῆρες δὲ κηραίνουσι καὶ βροτοί τιμήν [but beasts and mortals ravage its honor] (correctly βροτοί τί μιν [mortals ... it] Turnebus, except that he should have written viv) καὶ κνώδαλα πτεροῦντα καὶ πεδοστιβῆ, καρπώματα στάζοντα κηρύσσει Κύπρις | 5 | κάλωρα κωλύουσαν θωσ μένην (ει written above η) ἐρῶ [and winged creatures and those that walk the earth, Cypris proclaims the dripping fruits ... I will say ...], where Stanleius reads κάωρα, Canterus κάξωρα, which accomplishes nothing unless the following words have been emended, which no one has yet done.
tender fruit, but not at all well-guarded
M, but beasts and mortals ravage its honor
and winged creatures and those that walk the earth, Cypris proclaims the dripping fruits ... I will say
to the one who does not think well
for the most part war from the gods turns out well
so as not to think well
having fallen well in the slaughter
we will set them ruling this house well
pray that the rest turns out well
to those who died well there
so that it appears well to me
you guard the things in the house well
you inquire about my father well
fruit, bearing all things not to fare well
so that these things without harm – will end well
these things would benefit us well
the one who is well blessed
He mentioned the torches and poles in the Xantriae (fr. 167).
in the preliminary rites of the pole
He mentioned the torches and poles in the Xantriae
the toil of the compass, finger-pointed
and he rests the toil of the horses
and may they not have the farthest gleam of the furnace
